ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a signal flow graph from left to right, and the main path nodes are successively X1, X2, X3, X4, X5. The gains on the main path are labeled a, b, c, d in sequence, so the single forward path gain from X1 to X5 is abcd. The figure also has three backward feedback branches, which form loops with the main-path branches b, c, d respectively, and are labeled e, f, g. Reasoning: According to Mason's formula, the single forward path P = abcd. The gains of the individual loops are be, cf, dg. Among pairs of non-touching loops, only be and dg do not touch each other, so the product bedg of the two enters Δ with a positive sign. Thus Δ = 1 - (be + cf + dg) + bedg. Since all loops touch this forward path, the Δ1 corresponding to this path is 1. Therefore X5/X1 = PΔ1/Δ = abcd/[1 - (be + cf + dg) + bedg].

raw_record.question_text: Consider the signal flow graph shown in the image. What is the gain \( \frac{X_5}{X_1} \)?

method.method_draft: Use Mason's formula. From the image, take the single forward path from X1 to X5 as a-b-c-d, so P = abcd. Enumerate individual loops: b followed by feedback e gives be; c followed by feedback f gives cf; d followed by feedback g gives dg. The only pair of non-touching loops is be and dg, so their product contributes +bedg. Thus Delta = 1 - (be + cf + dg) + bedg and the requested gain is X5/X1 = abcd / [1 - (be + cf + dg) + bedg].
